viewer.hints: 1 Text · 2 Binary · 3 Hex · 4 Image · 5 Markdown · A/S/6/8/E Encoding · W Wrap · F7 Search · Ctrl+wheel/+/-/0 Text size · N/P Next/Previous · Esc Close
viewer.search_placeholder: Search for text, or hex bytes such as 4F 6B 0A
viewer.bad_offset: Enter an offset such as 0x1F, $1F, 1Fh or 31.
viewer.quick_nothing: Quick View shows the file under the cursor of the other panel.
error.image_too_large: The image is too large to show.
error.image_broken: The image cannot be shown: the file is damaged or its format is not supported.
archive.test.result: Archive test of {name} {state}: {passed} OK, {damaged} damaged, {encrypted} encrypted (not tested){first}
setting.archive.enter_opens.help: On: Enter on a .zip, .7z or .tar file shows its contents in the panel. Off: the system opens it. Ctrl+PageDown always opens an archive in the panel.
setting.archive.decoder_memory_mib.help: The most memory unpacking an .xz, .tar.xz or .7z file may set aside for its dictionary. A file whose header asks for more is refused before anything is reserved, so a crafted archive of a few bytes cannot take gigabytes. 256 MiB is more than any xz or 7-Zip preset uses. Counts for archives opened from now on.
setting.checksum.enter_verifies.help: On: Enter or a double click on a .sfv, .md5, .sha, .sha1, .sha256, .sha512, .b3 or .blake3 file checks the files it lists. Off: the system opens it. Ctrl+Shift+F10 always checks it.
setting.selection.include_folders: Num+, Num- and Shift+F2 select folders too
setting.selection.include_folders.help: On: Num+ and Num- also select and deselect folders whose names fit the mask (*.* takes every folder), and Shift+F2 also selects the folders only one side has. A mask ending in \ always means folders only.
setting.selection.space_moves_down: Space moves the cursor to the next entry
setting.selection.space_moves_down.help: On: Space selects the entry under the cursor and moves on to the next one, as Insert does. Off: the cursor stays on the entry. A folder is counted either way.
setting.mouse.click_clears_marks: A click clears the selection (as in Explorer)
setting.mouse.click_clears_marks.help: Off: a click in a file list only moves the cursor and the selection stays, as in Total Commander. On: a click also clears the selection, as in Windows Explorer. Ctrl+click and Shift+click select either way.
error.archive_read_only: Archives are changed only by adding to them (F5) and deleting from them (F8); unpack an archive to change it otherwise.
error.not_an_archive: This file is not an archive rCommander can open.
archive_ops.each_own: &Each entry into an archive of its own
archive_ops.confirm_overwrite: The archive exists already. Replace it?
archive_ops.confirm_delete: The packed files are deleted once the archive is complete. Continue?
archive_ops.own_folder: Unpack each archive into a folder of its &own
archive_ops.password_wrong: The password was wrong. Try again.
archive_ops.password_note: The password is used for this archive only and is not stored. Cancel skips the encrypted files.
error.unsafe_entry: Skipped: the name in the archive would leave the target folder or cannot be stored safely.
error.link_not_extracted: Skipped: links stored in an archive are not created.
error.pack_failed: The archive could not be written: the archive writer stopped unexpectedly. Nothing was left under its name.
setting.terminal.follow_panel.help: Turning to the terminal, or moving the panel while it shows the terminal, changes the shell's folder too - only while the shell waits at an empty prompt, never into a running program.
setting.terminal.panel_follows.help: Turning back to the files shows the folder the shell was last in.
setting.terminal.end_programs_on_close: End programs started in a terminal with it
setting.terminal.end_programs_on_close.h: On, closing a terminal - or rCommander - also ends what its shell started, such as ssh, a build or a window opened from it, so nothing keeps running unseen. Off, only the shell ends and programs started from it keep running. Windows; elsewhere closing the terminal hangs them up.
setting.terminal.copy_ctrl_c.help: On, Ctrl+C copies the text selected in a terminal and clears the selection; with nothing selected it interrupts the running program as always. Off, Ctrl+C always interrupts; Ctrl+Shift+C copies either way.
setting.terminal.copy_right_click.help: On, a right click copies the text selected in a terminal and clears the selection; with nothing selected it pastes (Windows). Off, a right click always pastes.
setting.terminal.copy_on_select: Copy text as soon as it is selected
setting.terminal.copy_on_select.help: On, letting go of the mouse after selecting text in a terminal copies it at once. Off, selected text is copied with Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Shift+C or a right click.
setting.terminal.osc52_copy: Programs may copy to the clipboard
setting.terminal.osc52_copy.help: On, a program in a terminal - also on a server you are connected to - may put text on the clipboard (OSC 52), as Claude Code does with what you select in it. Programs can never read the clipboard this way. Off, such copies are dropped.
setting.terminal.osc52_remote: Programs on a server may copy to the clipboard
setting.terminal.osc52_remote.help: On, a program in an SSH terminal may put text on the clipboard too (OSC 52), as in Windows Terminal. Off, only the programs of local and WSL terminals may. Either way only the terminal a panel shows sets the clipboard, with at most 1 MiB of text, and the status line says which one did.
setting.terminal.shift_selects: Shift with the mouse selects text
setting.terminal.shift_selects.help: On, holding Shift while you select with the mouse selects text in the terminal even when a program such as Claude Code or vim takes the mouse; Ctrl+C or a right click then copies it. Off, the mouse always goes to such a program.
setting.terminal.paste_image: Ctrl+Alt+V pastes an image as a file path
setting.terminal.paste_image.help: On, the key (Ctrl+Alt+V unless changed in Shortcuts) saves the clipboard's image as a PNG file where the terminal's program can read it - the temp folder, the same file under /mnt for WSL, /tmp on an SSH server, uploaded without asking - and pastes its path, for Claude Code and other programs that read images from a path. The files are removed when the terminal closes. Off, the key does nothing.
setting.terminal.paste_ctrl_v.help: On, Ctrl+V pastes the text on the clipboard into a terminal; with no text on it - an image, say - Ctrl+V goes to the running program, which may paste the image itself. Off, Ctrl+V always goes to the program; Ctrl+Shift+V and a right click paste either way.
setting.terminal.shell_integration.help: New shells (PowerShell, bash, zsh, cmd) report their folder and prompt to rCommander; without it neither direction follows. Applies to shells started from now on.
terminal.follow.no_integration: The shell does not report its prompt, so it stays in its folder (shell integration is off or not supported).
terminal.follow.running: A program runs in the shell; it changes to the panel's folder at the next prompt.
terminal.follow.line_not_empty: The shell's command line is not empty; it changes to the panel's folder at the next prompt.
terminal.follow.unreachable: The shell cannot change to this folder.
terminal.follow.other_system: This folder belongs to another system than the shell (Windows or a WSL distribution), so the shell stays where it is. The terminal key opens a fitting shell.
error.symlink_privilege: Windows creates symbolic links only in Developer Mode or with administrator rights. Turn on Developer Mode in the Windows settings, or create a junction (folders) or a shortcut instead.
error.drive_timed_out: The drive or share did not answer in time. Escape stops a folder that keeps the panel waiting.
error.device_unavailable: The device does not share its files. Unlock it and choose "File transfer" in its USB settings, or plug it in again.
error.property_invalid: This cannot be done with what was given.
connections.title: Connections
connections.empty: No connections yet. Insert adds one, F7 a folder.
connections.keys: Enter opens a folder, F2 renames, F7 new folder, F8 deletes, Insert new connection, Shift+F5 duplicates, Space shows it in the drive bar, Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down move, Ctrl+Left and Ctrl+Right outdent and indent, Shift+F10 opens the menu, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+V move to another folder, typing filters, Tab goes to the form.
connections.folder_on_bar_help: The drive bar shows the folder as a button that opens a menu of all its servers, those in its subfolders too. Folders of the top level are shown unless you switch them off.
connections.credential_user: Left empty, it logs in as {user}, the credential's user.
connections.delete_credential: Delete the credential {name}? {connections} connections use it and fall back to their own user and secrets.
connections.name: Name
connections.delete_folder: Delete the folder {name} with {folders} folders and {connections} connections inside it, and their stored secrets?
connections.delete_connection: Delete the connection {name} and its stored secrets?
connections.cut: Cut. Choose a folder and press Ctrl+V to move it there.
connections.certificate_none: No certificate is trusted for this server yet; the first FTPS connection asks.
connections.choose: Choose a connection in the tree, or press Insert for a new one.
connections.field.name: Name
connections.import_key: Take the key file into the vault when saving
connections.forget.totp_seed: Remove the stored one-time code seed
connections.secret_note: A stored secret is never shown; what you type is stored encrypted when you save.
connections.totp_hint: Paste the otpauth:// link or the Base32 secret from the authenticator setup. rCommander answers the server's question for a verification code with the current code.
connections.secret_locked: The vault is locked: what you type stays hidden.
connections.source.title: Secret source
connections.tested: The connection works: it logged in with what is stored.
connections.invalid: Some fields need a correction; nothing was saved.
connections.vault.create_help: Stored passwords and keys are encrypted with it. It cannot be recovered: without it the stored secrets are lost. At least 8 characters.
connections.vault.unlock_help: Enter the master password to store the secret.
connections.import.title: Import from ssh config
connections.import.help: Hosts of ~/.ssh/config (or a file in ~/.ssh/config.d) become connections. Key files stay paths unless you take them into the vault. ProxyJump to one host of the file becomes its jump host, LocalForward a port forward that does not start by itself; patterns, Match blocks and lists of jump hosts are not imported.
connections.import.no_hosts: The file names no host to import.
connections.import.key_taken: {host}: the key is in the vault.
connections.import.keys_failed: {count} keys could not be taken into the vault.
tc_import.title: Import from Total Commander
tc_import.help: The directory hotlist, the folder tabs, the list colours (light and dark), the colours by file type and the file list font of wincmd.ini, and the FTP, FTPS and SFTP connections of wcx_ftp.ini. Hotlist entries and connections go into folders named Imported from Total Commander, colour rules are added after yours; a second import adds nothing twice. Programs, internal commands and plugin folders of the hotlist are not imported. Total Commander's files are only read.
tc_import.passwords_hint: Passwords are taken only when you tick the box: straight into the vault, encrypted with your master password. A password Total Commander protects with its own master password cannot be read; enter it again in the connection.
tc_import.skip.internal_command: Runs a Total Commander command; not imported.
tc_import.skip.server_path: A server address; connections come from wcx_ftp.ini.
tc_import.skip.plugin_path: A file-system plugin's folder; not imported.
tc_import.skip.relative_path: Not a full path; not imported.
tc_import.skip.unknown_variable: Uses an environment variable the import does not read (only those Total Commander uses in paths).
tc_import.skip.name_invalid: The name is empty or too long.
tc_import.skip.protocol_unknown: A protocol rCommander does not speak.
tc_import.skip.port_invalid: The port is not a number from 1 to 65535.
tc_import.skip.inverse: An inverted cursor or selection; rCommander has no such setting.
tc_import.skip.search_filter: Colours by a saved search; rCommander colours by file mask only.
tc_import.skip.too_many: More than 64 colour rules; not imported.
tc_import.warning.wincmd_not_found: No wincmd.ini was found; name the file.
tc_import.warning.ftp_ini_not_found: No wcx_ftp.ini was found; name the file to import connections.
tc_import.warning.value_too_long: Some values were too long and were skipped.
tc_import.warning.dir_menu_redirected: The hotlist is kept in another file (RedirectSection); it is not imported.
tc_import.password_skip.master_password: protected by Total Commander's master password; enter it again
tc_import.password_skip.unreadable: the password could not be read; enter it again
tc_import.password_skip.anonymous: an anonymous connection needs no password
connections.vault.needed_help: A connection needs a stored password or key. Enter the master password; the connection tries again once the vault is open.
error.certificate_changed: This server presented a different certificate than the trusted one. The connection was stopped.
error.certificate_expired: The trusted certificate of this server has expired. Decide about it in rCommander.
error.ftp_plaintext_unconfirmed: This FTP server is not encrypted: the password would cross the network in clear. Allow it in rCommander first.
error.certificate_question_not_found: This certificate question is no longer open.
error.certificate_unreadable: This certificate cannot be read. It can be accepted once, but not stored.
error.trusted_certificate_not_found: This trusted certificate no longer exists.
certs.unknown_text: The system does not trust the certificate this server presented - common for NAS devices, routers and self-hosted services that sign their own. Compare the fingerprint with the one the server's administrator gave you, and trust the certificate only if they match.
certs.changed_title: WARNING: the server's certificate has changed
certs.changed_text: The server presented a different certificate than the one you trusted for it. Someone may be intercepting the connection, or the server got a new certificate. The connection was stopped. If you know why it changed, remove the trusted certificate in the connection manager and connect again.
certs.expired_title: WARNING: the trusted certificate has expired
certs.expired_text: This is the certificate you trusted for the server, but its validity has ended. Accept it once only if you know why the server still uses it; ask its administrator to renew it.
certs.subject: Subject
certs.unreadable: The certificate's subject and validity cannot be read.
certs.waiting: Certificate questions waiting after this one: {count}
certs.info_once: The certificate of {host} is accepted for the next connection only. Connect again.
certs.info_saved: The certificate of {host} is trusted and saved. Connect again.
certs.info_cancelled: Not connected to {host}: its certificate was not accepted.
certs.plaintext_text: This connection uses plain FTP without TLS: your user name, your password and every file cross the network unencrypted, readable by anyone on the way. Send them only on a network you trust, and use FTPS where the server offers it.
certs.plaintext_info_once: The password may go to {host} in clear for the next connection only. Connect again.
certs.plaintext_info_always: The password may go to {host} in clear until rCommander closes. Connect again.
certs.plaintext_info_cancelled: Not connected to {host}: no password was sent.
multi_rename.title: Multi-rename
multi_rename.ph_first_upper: first letter of each word upper case from here
multi_rename.ph_case_as_is: case as it is from here
multi_rename.find_hint: Several terms separated by |; * and ? as wildcards
multi_rename.case_words_upper: First Letter Of Each Word Uppercase
multi_rename.preset_name_needed: Type a name for the preset first.
multi_rename.log_path: Full path of the log file
multi_rename.log_absolute: The log needs the full path of a file.
multi_rename.log_failed: The log could not be written: {error}
multi_rename.changes: {count} of {total} entries get a new name.
multi_rename.conflicts: {count} conflicts among {changes} new names; nothing can be renamed until they are solved.
multi_rename.stopped: The rename stopped before its end; Undo reverses what was done.
multi_rename.rolled_back: The rename failed and was undone: every name is as before. The first error: {error}
multi_rename.parked: The rename stopped. These files are under temporary names: {names}. Undo puts them back.
multi_rename.undo_stopped: The undo stopped before its end; Undo again continues it.
multi_rename.nothing: Select the files to rename, or put the cursor on one.
multi_rename.panel_moved: The panel is on another drive now; close the dialog and open it again.
drag.failed: The files could not be dragged out of rCommander.
drag.fetched_hint: The files are in a temporary folder now; drag them out again.
drag.needs_local: Remote files leave rCommander through a temporary folder; show a local folder in the other panel first.
drag.no_temp: No temporary folder could be made for the remote files.
drag.fetch_question: {count} entries ({size}) are downloaded to a temporary folder before they leave rCommander.
drag.fetch_question_unknown: {count} entries, with folders of unknown size, are downloaded to a temporary folder before they leave rCommander.
drag.fetch_note: The temporary copies are deleted when rCommander closes.
drop.busy: Close the open dialog first, then drop the files again.
drop.files_only: Files can be dropped onto a file list only.
drop.refused: {count} of the dropped or pasted paths were not taken.
drop.needs_local: Files go into a remote folder only while the other panel shows a local one.
clipboard.cut_remote: Remote files cannot be cut; copy them with Ctrl+C.
clipboard.failed: The clipboard could not be written.
compare.title: Compare by content
compare.binary: Binary or too large to compare line by line; compared byte by byte.
compare.first_difference: First difference at byte {offset} ({hex}): left {left}, right {right}
sync.title: Synchronize directories
sync.invalid_tolerance: The time tolerance must be a whole number of seconds.
sync.idle: Compare the two folders to see what differs.
sync.found: {equal} equal, {different} different, {left_only} only left, {right_only} only right. Click an action or press Space to change it.
sync.confirm_copy_right: Copy {files} files ({size}) from left to right
sync.confirm_copy_left: Copy {files} files ({size}) from right to left
sync.confirm_deletes: Delete {right} entries on the right and {left} on the left
sync.confirm_permanent: Delete &permanently, not into the recycle bin
settings.import.total_commander_help: The directory hotlist, the folder tabs and the FTP, FTPS and SFTP connections. A preview shows what is found; nothing is imported before you choose Import.
settings.import.rcommander_help: Export settings, connections, trusted host keys and certificates, the hotlist and tabs to a file, encrypted with an export password of its own, and import them on another computer. Apply or cancel changes here first: the export and import open in the main window.
network.no_letter: Every drive letter is in use.
network.map_note: Windows asks for the user name and password itself and keeps them in its Credential Manager; rCommander never sees them.
network.waiting: Waiting for Windows - it may be asking for the user name and password.
network.unmap_text: Disconnect the chosen network drive? Windows forgets it for the next sign-in too.
network.in_use: Files on {drive} are open. Disconnecting anyway may lose unsaved changes in the programs that have them open.
error.network_path_invalid: This is not a network folder. Write it as \\server\share.
error.drive_letter_invalid: Choose a drive letter from A to Z.
error.drive_letter_in_use: A drive already has this letter. Choose a free one.
error.drive_not_network: This drive is not a network drive.
error.network_drive_in_use: Files on the network drive are open.
error.network_path_not_found: The server or the share cannot be found. Check the name and the network.
error.network_credentials_conflict: Windows is already connected to this server as another user. Disconnect that connection first.
error.network_access_denied: The server refused access for this user.
error.network_drives_unsupported: Network drives can only be mapped on Windows.
error.network_drive_failed: Windows could not complete the request.
settings.about.version_copied: Version info copied to the clipboard.
settings.about.link_not_opened: The browser could not be started; the address was copied to the clipboard instead.
settings.about.author: Author
settings.about.thanks: rCommander is built on many open-source projects; the Licences tab lists every one with its licence. Thank you to all who made them.
settings.about.licenses.help: The Rust crates rCommander is built from, with the licence each declares.
settings.about.licenses.name: Name
setting.columns.ext_width.help: In pixels at the default font size, 24 to 640; both file lists, scaled with their font. Drag the gap left of a column's title to change it, double-click it for the default.
setting.columns.size_width.help: In pixels at the default font size, 40 to 640; both file lists, scaled with their font.
setting.columns.packed_width.help: Inside an archive; in pixels at the default font size, 40 to 640.
setting.columns.date_width.help: In pixels at the default font size, 48 to 640; both file lists, scaled with their font.
setting.columns.rights_width.help: On a server; in pixels at the default font size, 40 to 640.
setting.panels.split_permille.help: Of the width of both panels, in tenths of a percent, 100 to 900; 500 is half. Drag the gap between the panels to change it, double-click it for half.
panel.reading: Reading the folder: {count} entries so far
setting.columns.owner.help: Shows user and group in the file lists where they are known: on an SFTP server, and local folders on Linux and macOS.
setting.columns.owner_width.help: In pixels at the default font size, 40 to 640; both file lists, scaled with their font.
error.rdm_path_refused: Only a file ending in .rdm can be imported.
error.rdm_too_large: The export is too large to import (more than 16 MiB).
error.rdm_encrypted: This export is protected with a master key, or is not an export of Remote Desktop Manager. Export again without a master key.
error.rdm_invalid: The export is not valid XML, or declares a DTD, which the import does not read.
error.rdm_not_an_export: This file is not an export of Remote Desktop Manager.
error.rdm_not_supported: Not supported: rCommander has no connection of this kind.
error.rdm_not_supported_yet: Not supported yet: FTP and FTPS entries will follow.
error.rdm_no_id: The entry has no ID, so a later import could not find it again.
error.rdm_duplicate_id: Another entry of the export has the same ID.
error.rdm_folder_invalid: A folder name holds a control character.
error.rdm_value_too_long: A name, folder, host or user is too long.
rdm_import.title: Import from Remote Desktop Manager
rdm_import.help: The SSH connections of an export of Remote Desktop Manager (.rdm, exported without a master key). They go into Imported from Remote Desktop Manager, RDM's folders inside; a second import adds nothing twice and updates host, port, user and key path. FTP and FTPS entries follow later; RDP, VNC, web and other entries are not imported. The file is only read.
rdm_import.passwords_hint: Passwords are not imported: Remote Desktop Manager keeps them obfuscated with its own scheme. Enter them again in the connection, where they go into the vault.
rdm_import.key_path_refused: key file not taken (not a local path)
rdm_import.too_many_entries: The export holds more entries than the import reads; the rest was left out.
settings.host_keys.help: The SSH host keys and FTPS certificates you trusted. A new or changed key is trusted only in the question of the connection that meets it; after Remove, the next connection to that server asks again.
settings.host_keys.none: No host key or certificate is trusted yet.
settings.host_keys.confirm_key: Remove the trusted host key of {server}? The next connection to it asks again.
settings.host_keys.confirm_certificate: Remove the trusted certificate of {server}? The next connection to it asks again.
settings.host_keys.removed: Removed. The next connection to the server asks again.
settings.host_keys.confirm_revoked: Remove the revocation of the key {fingerprint}? A server that presents it is then judged like any other key.
settings.host_keys.unrevoked: Revocation removed. The key is judged like any other key again.
settings.host_keys.imported: Imported from {path}: {added} new, {unchanged} already trusted, {conflicts} changed (the trusted key stays), {skipped} skipped.
error.key_path_refused: Only a key file on this computer or in a WSL distribution is taken into the vault, not one on a network share.
setting.panels.drive_line_volume: Volume name in the drive line
setting.panels.drive_line_volume.help: Shows the drive's volume name in brackets after the drive, a server's or WSL distribution's name for those.
setting.panels.drive_line_buttons: Root and up buttons in the drive line
setting.panels.drive_line_buttons.help: Ends each panel's drive line with \ (to the drive's root) and .. (one folder up).
setting.viewer.markdown_preview: Show Markdown files as a preview
setting.viewer.markdown_preview.help: Lister (F3) and Quick View (Ctrl+Q) show a .md or .markdown file formatted; 5 switches between the preview and the text. Off: such files open as text, and 5 still shows the preview. Images are never loaded, HTML in the file is shown as text, and only http, https and mailto links open, on a click.
setting.viewer.markdown_select: Select and copy in the Markdown preview
setting.viewer.markdown_select.help: The mouse selects text in the preview, also across paragraphs, lists, tables and code; Shift+click extends, a double click takes a word, a triple click a line. Ctrl+A selects all, Ctrl+C copies the selection as plain text. Applies to files opened afterwards.
setting.viewer.markdown_code_highlight: Colour code blocks in the Markdown preview
setting.viewer.markdown_code_highlight.h: A code block whose tag names a language (```rust, ```json, ```sh, ```python, ```sql and other common ones) shows keywords, strings, numbers and comments in the theme's colours. A block without a tag or with an unknown one stays plain; a block over 64 KiB stays plain. Applies to files opened afterwards.
setting.viewer.picture_megapixels: Largest picture shown at full detail (megapixels)
setting.viewer.picture_megapixels.help: A picture with more pixels is scaled down to this many before it is shown, so a very large photo or scan opens without using gigabytes of memory; zoom and the status line still go by its own size. Higher is sharper when you zoom in.
viewer.link_refused: Not opened: {url} - only http, https and mailto links open.
viewer.link_failed: The system did not take the link.
error.markdown_too_large: The file is over 4 MiB: shown as text instead of the Markdown preview.
error.markdown_broken: The Markdown preview cannot be made: shown as text.
error.viewer_copy_too_large: The file is over 4 MiB: its whole text is not copied. Select a part with the mouse.
setting.drives.follow_on_own_drive: A drive letter in the command line (such as d:) follows the other panel on the same drive too
setting.drives.follow_on_own_drive.help: On: a drive letter in the command line (such as d:) opens the other panel's folder even when this panel is already on that drive, at another folder, as in Total Commander. The drive bar and the drive menu leave a panel on its own drive where it is. Works only while "A drive change goes to the other panel's folder" is on.
setting.drives.portable_devices: Show portable devices in the drive bar
setting.drives.portable_devices.help: On: phones, tablets and cameras connected over USB (MTP) appear in the drive bar under their own name; their files can be read, copied both ways and deleted, and new folders created on them. Off: the system is not asked for them.
setting.drives.follow_other_panel: A drive change goes to the other panel's folder
setting.drives.follow_other_panel.help: On: changing to the drive the other panel shows (drive bar, drive menu, or a drive letter in the command line such as d:) opens the other panel's folder, as in Total Commander. Off: the folder this panel last showed on that drive, else the drive's root.
setting.sort.names.help: Like Windows and Total Commander: upper and lower case alike, symbols before digits before letters, hyphens and apostrophes only between otherwise equal names. Like Linux: the byte order of ls in the C locale, capitals first. By the panel's target: Windows' order on this computer's drives, Linux' on SSH and FTP servers and inside WSL.
setting.sort.numbers_by_value.help: On: file2 comes before file10, as in Total Commander and the Explorer. Off: digits compare as characters, file10 before file2.
setting.keys.underline_access_keys.help: On: the underlined letters of the dialogs' buttons always show. Off: they show while Alt is held, as in Windows. Alt with the letter presses the button either way; the letter alone does while a button or checkbox has the focus ring.
setting.tabs.drag_reorder.help: On: a tab dragged within its tab bar goes where it is dropped, as in Total Commander; a click still shows it, Escape cancels the drag. Off: a press on a tab only shows it. In the list of tabs (Ctrl+Shift+A) Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down move a tab either way.
setting.keys.context_menu_shortcuts.help: On: the menus rCommander draws - a tab's, the file list's own, the queue's - show each entry's key on the right, as Windows menus do. Off: the entries' names only.
setting.keys.macos_cmd_as_ctrl: Cmd works as Ctrl on macOS
setting.keys.macos_cmd_as_ctrl.help: On: Cmd does what Ctrl does in the keymap (Cmd+R refreshes, Cmd+Shift+P opens the command palette), Ctrl still works, and keys show with the Cmd symbol. Off: only Ctrl is Ctrl, a key pressed with Cmd is left to the system, and keys show with the Control symbol. Only on macOS.
setting.keys.overrides.help: Your changes to the standard keys, as the Shortcuts tab writes them: Ctrl+K=copy gives Ctrl+K the copy, F5= takes F5 away, Ctrl+1=theme:dark:nord-dark switches to the dark Nord theme.
setting.viewer.dos_extensions.help: File extensions without dots, separated by spaces. Lister (F3) and Quick View (Ctrl+Q) show such files in the DOS character set, with its box-drawing art, and without wrapping; a file with a byte-order mark, in UTF-16 or in UTF-8 beyond plain ASCII keeps its own encoding. In the viewer S switches to DOS and A back to ANSI. Empty: no file opens as DOS text.
setting.viewer.dos_tight_lines: Let the blocks of DOS art touch
setting.viewer.dos_tight_lines.help: DOS text - an .nfo, a .diz, or any file switched to DOS with S - draws its lines exactly as tall as the viewer font's full block, so the block characters of its art join without gaps, as in Total Commander's Lister. Off: its lines are as tall as any other text's.
setting.viewer.text_zoom: Ctrl+wheel, Ctrl++ and Ctrl+- change the viewer's text size
setting.viewer.text_zoom.help: In Lister (F3) and Quick View (Ctrl+Q) the text, binary, hex and Markdown views get a step larger or smaller, from 6 to 72 points; Ctrl+0 goes back to the viewer font size. In the image view the same keys zoom the picture and Ctrl+0 fits it to the window. Off: Ctrl+wheel scrolls, and in Quick View Ctrl+Num+ and Ctrl+Num- select and deselect all as in the panels.
setting.viewer.text_zoom_keep.help: This window only: the size stays with that viewer window and the files N and P step to, or with Quick View while its cursor moves; the next viewer opens at the viewer font size. Saved: every change is stored as the viewer font size, so every viewer opens at it, and Ctrl+0 stores the default 13.
setting.viewer.text_zoom_keep.window: Applies to this viewer window only
setting.viewer.text_zoom_keep.setting: Is saved as the viewer font size
viewer.text_size_saved: Text size {size} pt - saved as the viewer font size
setting.plugins.viewer_token_colors: Show a viewer plugin's text in colour
setting.plugins.viewer_token_colors.help: A viewer plugin can show a file as coloured text, as an editor does - keys, strings, numbers and comments each in their own colour. The colours are the theme's, in light and in dark; the plugin only says what each part is. Off: the same text without colour. The hex and binary views never show colour.
viewer.tree_empty: The document has nothing to show as a tree.
viewer.status_tree_full: Tree · {nodes} nodes - the tree takes no more
viewer.hints_views: 1 Text · 2 Binary · 3 Hex · 4 Image · 5 Markdown · 7 Next view · A/S/6/8/E Encoding · W Wrap · F7 Search · Ctrl+wheel/+/-/0 Text size · N/P Next/Previous · Esc Close
setting.plugins.enabled.help: Off: no plugin runs, and the built-in viewer shows every file. The plugins stay installed and keep their own switches.
setting.plugins.crash_limit: Failures before a plugin is suspended
setting.plugins.crash_limit.help: A plugin that crashes, hangs or runs out of memory this many times within five minutes is suspended until you resume it on this page (1-10).
setting.plugins.viewer_output_limit_mib: Largest text a viewer plugin may write (MiB)
A viewer plugin's text output stops at this size (1-4096 MiB); the viewer shows what came so far.
setting.plugins.associations.help: Pairs such as csv=<plugin id>, separated by spaces: that plugin shows the extension, ahead of what the plugins claim. Built-in formats come first. Empty: the plugins' own claims.
setting.plugins.development_mode.help: For plugin authors: unsigned packages can be installed and run, marked as unsigned everywhere. Leave it off otherwise - a signature is what tells you who made a plugin.
setting.plugins.recent_calls_shown.help: How many of a plugin's latest calls its details list, behind a click, and how many plugins_list answers with over MCP. 0 leaves the list out; the summary of the calls stays.
settings.colours.no_rules: No rule yet: every name in the list's text colour.
settings.colours.low_text: The text is hard to read on the background (contrast below 4.5:1).
settings.colours.low_stripe: The text is hard to read on the second background (contrast below 4.5:1).
settings.colours.low_cursor: The cursor text is hard to read on the cursor (contrast below 4.5:1).
settings.colours.low_marked: Marked names are hard to read on the background (contrast below 4.5:1).
settings.shortcuts.help: Every key rCommander runs. Select a row, then change its key, give it another one, remove it or reset it; changed rows are marked. Locked keys belong to the window - hover over one to see why. The changes count from OK or Apply.
settings.shortcuts.recording: Press the new key for "{name}" - Esc cancels.
settings.shortcuts.conflict: {key} runs "{holder}" now. Give it to "{name}" instead?
settings.shortcuts.unknown: this version has no such action.
settings.shortcuts.locked.focus: Tab walks the controls of a dialog; the window keeps it.
settings.shortcuts.locked.escape: Escape closes a dialog and stops a wait; the window keeps it.
settings.shortcuts.locked.access_key: Alt with a letter or digit opens the menus and presses a dialog's buttons; the window keeps it.
settings.shortcuts.locked.window: The window handles this key itself; it cannot move.
settings.shortcuts.theme.help: Choose the theme, press Record key, then the key that switches to it.
settings.plugins.help: Plugins are signed packages (.rcplug) that run in a sandbox: no files, no network, no secrets - only the file they are shown. Install one from a package you trust; you see what it asks for before anything is installed.
settings.plugins.key_trusted: Signed by a key you trust.
settings.plugins.key_untrusted: Signed by a key you have not trusted yet. Compare this fingerprint with the one its author publishes; installing trusts the key for this author's plugins:
settings.plugins.key_mismatch: Signed by another key than the one you trusted under this key id: it cannot be installed.
settings.plugins.key_revoked: Signed by a revoked key: it cannot be installed.
settings.plugins.key_unsigned: Not signed: only development mode installs it, and it stays marked as unsigned.
settings.plugins.installed_versions: Installed already: {versions}. The new version runs from the next start.
settings.plugins.withdrawn: This version was withdrawn: it cannot be installed.
settings.plugins.name: Name
error.plugins_unavailable: Plugins are not available in this run.
error.plugin_not_found: No plugin with this id is installed.
error.secret_source_locked: The secret source is locked. Unlock the password manager and try again.
error.secret_source_unreachable: The secret source does not answer. Start the password manager's service.
error.secret_source_unlicensed: The secret source has no valid licence.
error.secret_source_failed: The secret source failed. Its plugin page shows its latest calls.
error.secret_source_entry_missing: The secret source has no such entry any more. Pick the entry again in the connection.
error.secret_source_missing: The secret source is not installed or is switched off.
error.secret_source_invalid: This entry cannot be used as a secret source.
error.plugin_no_previous_version: There is no older version of this plugin to go back to.
error.plugin_setting_refused: The plugin does not have this setting, or does not take this value.
error.plugin_folder_failed: The plugin folder could not be read or written.
error.plugin_key_untrusted: The package is signed by a key you have not trusted. Install it from its preview to trust the key.
error.plugin_invalid: This is no plugin rCommander can use: the package or its component is not valid.
error.plugin_denied: The plugin reaches for more than its manifest grants, and is refused.
error.plugin_unsigned: The package is not signed. Only development mode installs unsigned plugins.
error.plugin_signature_invalid: The package was changed after it was signed: its signature does not hold.
error.plugin_key_mismatch: The package names a key id you trusted for another key.
error.plugin_key_revoked: The package is signed by a revoked key.
error.plugin_digest_revoked: This version of the plugin was withdrawn.
error.plugin_needs_newer_app: The plugin needs a newer rCommander.
error.plugin_version_installed: This version of the plugin is installed already.
error.plugin_version_in_use: This version is in use by an open viewer. Close it, then remove the version.
viewer.plugin_failed: {plugin} could not show this file: {reason} The built-in viewer shows it.
error.plugin_failed: The plugin could not read the file.
error.plugin_crashed: The plugin stopped with an error.
error.plugin_out_of_fuel: The plugin used up its computing budget.
error.plugin_out_of_memory: The plugin needed more memory than it may use.
error.plugin_suspended: The plugin is suspended after repeated failures; resume it in Settings → Plugins.
error.plugin_bad_output: The plugin answered something rCommander does not accept.
error.plugin_output_too_large: The plugin's output is larger than the viewer's output limit in Settings → Plugins.
error.plugin_write_too_large: The plugin wrote more at once than it may.
error.plugin_sink_failed: The plugin's output could not be written.
error.plugin_source_failed: The file could not be read for the plugin.
error.plugin_unknown_handle: The plugin used a file it was not given.
error.plugin_session_closed: The plugin stopped; open the file again.
error.plugin_output_not_offered: The plugin offers nothing the viewer can show.
error.plugin_request_too_large: The viewer asked the plugin for more than it may at once.
error.plugin_unknown_node: The plugin does not know this part of the tree.
error.plugin_tree_too_deep: The tree is nested deeper than the viewer shows.
error.plugin_host_failed: rCommander could not run the plugin.
error.plugin_http_denied: The plugin tried to reach an address it was not allowed.
error.plugin_http_failed: The plugin could not reach its service: nothing answered on the address it was allowed.
error.plugin_http_too_large: The plugin's service answered more than the plugin may read.
error.plugin_http_time_budget: The plugin's requests to its service took too long together; the call was ended.
error.text_too_long: A name, host or user name can be at most 255 characters long.
error.path_too_long: A key file path or start directory can be at most 4096 characters long.
ssh_import.warning.include_repeated: This Include names a file that was already read; each file is read once.
ssh_import.warning.too_many_includes: More than 256 files are included; this Include and every later one are skipped.
ssh_import.warning.too_many_hosts: More than 1024 hosts are named; this one and every later new one are not imported.
error.rename_name_direction: The new name contains a character that turns the reading direction, so it would read as another name.
error.plugin_key_changed: This plugin is installed already, signed by another key. Remove the installed plugin before installing this package.
settings.plugins.key_changed: Signed by another key than the installed plugin of this name: it cannot be installed. Remove the installed plugin first if you trust this package.
setting.ssh.agent_max_keys: Most agent keys offered per login
setting.ssh.agent_max_keys.help: How many keys of the SSH agents one login offers, the connection's own key first. A server counts each key against its limit of tries and learns every key offered (1-20).
setting.connections.totp_autofill: Answer one-time code questions at the SSH login
setting.connections.totp_autofill.help: When a connection has a one-time code seed, rCommander answers the server's question for a verification code with the current code. Off, the question is left unanswered, as without a seed; a login script's Send one-time code step still sends it.
settings.not_saved: The settings were not all saved: {error}
setting.backup.keep.help: After each backup into the backup folder, the oldest backups with a generated name beyond this number are deleted. Backups you named yourself are never deleted.
error.plugin_package_changed: The package file changed after its preview. Preview it again before installing.
terminal.paste_control: The text to paste contains control characters (such as Ctrl+C) that act on the program. Paste anyway?
update.notice.on_quit: rCommander {version} is available and installs when you quit.
update.notice.failed: The update to {version} did not go ahead: {reason}
update.page.downloaded: Downloaded and checked; ready to install.
update.page.install_ends: Installing restarts rCommander: open terminals and SSH sessions end, the vault is locked after the restart, and MCP clients lose their connection for a moment. Tabs, folders and windows come back.
update.page.install_when_empty: Install once the queue is empty
update.page.install_after_download: Installs and restarts as soon as the download is complete and checked.
setting.update.check_enabled.help: A check asks the release host for one public file per channel, with the user agent rCommander/<version> and nothing else: no cookie, no installation id, nothing about the system or its use. The host sees the address, the time and the version. Check now always works.
setting.update.check_interval_hours.help: The first check comes a few minutes after the start, then one every so many hours (1 to 168).
setting.update.channel.help: Stable offers releases only; beta offers pre-releases too and the release that follows them. Until you choose, the channel of the running version applies. Nothing older than the running version is ever offered.
setting.update.source.help: Empty for the official GitHub releases. A mirror is an https:// folder serving rcommander-update-stable.json, rcommander-update-beta.json and the packages below it; its manifests are checked against the key built into rCommander all the same.
setting.update.proxy.help: Empty for the system's proxy (the Windows Internet options, HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY), direct for none, or http://host:port. No user name or password: a proxy that asks for a login is not supported; copy the download address instead.
setting.update.whats_new_after_update: Show what is new after an update
setting.update.whats_new_after_update.he: The first start after an update says so once; What's new opens the changelog.
setting.update.auto_install.help: Off: you install. When quitting (the default): a new version is downloaded in the background and installed as rCommander ends; the next start runs it, and a download not finished by then never holds up quitting. When idle: also restarts into it once nothing happened for the minutes below - no input, no job in the queue, no terminal or SSH session, no dialog. A version whose install failed is never installed by itself again.
setting.update.idle_minutes: Minutes without input before an idle update
setting.update.idle_minutes.help: How long nothing may happen before "when idle" restarts into the update (5 to 240).
setting.update.backup_retention_days: Days to keep the database copy after an update
setting.update.backup_retention_days.hel: Before every update the database is copied; after a proven update only the newest copy stays, and after these days it goes too. 0 keeps it for good.
error.update.not_configured: This build carries no update key; updates cannot be checked.
error.update.not_published: No update manifest is published for this channel yet.
error.update.fetch_failed: The release host could not be reached.
error.update.proxy_auth_required: The proxy asks for a login, which the update check does not give. Copy the download address instead.
error.update.too_large: The update manifest is too large and was refused.
error.update.malformed: The update manifest cannot be read.
error.update.untrusted: The update manifest is not signed by rCommander's update key.
error.update.bad_signature: The update manifest's signature does not verify; it was refused.
error.update.schema_version_unsupported: The update manifest is of a newer kind; update by hand once.
error.update.wrong_channel: The update manifest is for another channel and was refused.
error.update.stale: The update manifest is outdated or replayed and was refused.
error.update.invalid: The update manifest breaks a rule and was refused.
error.update.size_mismatch: The download has another size than the manifest says; it was deleted.
error.update.digest_mismatch: The download is not the file the manifest describes; it was deleted.
error.update.no_space: Not enough free space for the update (twice its size is needed).
error.update.not_started: Updates run in the rCommander window only.
error.update.no_artifact: The release has no package for this system.
error.update.install_unsupported: This installation does not update itself; download the package and unpack it by hand.
error.update.queue_busy: Jobs run or wait in the queue; the update installs once it is empty.
error.update.journal_invalid: The update journal names places outside this installation and was set aside.
error.update.install_dir_not_writable: The program folder cannot be written.
error.update.not_enough_space: The program folder's drive has not enough free space for the update.
error.update.archive_unknown: The update package is no archive rCommander knows.
error.update.archive_incomplete: The update package carries no rCommander program.
error.update.unpack_failed: The update package could not be unpacked.
error.update.switch_failed: The program files could not be replaced; the previous version is back.
error.update.start_failed: The new version did not start; the previous version is back.
error.update.new_version_exited: The new version ended right after its start; the previous version is back.
error.update.not_confirmed: The new version did not come up; the previous version is back.
error.update.confirm_timeout: The new version did not come up in time; the previous version is back.
error.update.app_did_not_end: rCommander did not end in time; nothing was changed.
error.update.updater_did_not_start: The updater did not start; nothing was changed.
error.update.interrupted: The update was interrupted; the previous version is in place.
error.update.rollback_failed: The previous version could not be put back completely; see Taking an update back by hand in the handbook.
error.update.instance_running: The previous version is back, but its database was not put back: another rCommander process (rcommander mcp) still had it open. End it, then see Taking an update back by hand in the handbook.
error.update.kind_marker: This installation was installed by an installer; update it there.
error.update.kind_no_version_file: This copy is no unpacked release package (no VERSION.txt beside it); download the package instead.
error.update.kind_not_writable: The program folder cannot be written; download the package instead.
error.update.kind_package_manager: This installation belongs to a package manager, which updates it: rCommander does not replace itself here, and installing updates by itself is off.
setting.appearance.theme_light.help: The colours rCommander draws with while the look is light, the terminals' included.
setting.appearance.theme_dark.help: The colours rCommander draws with while the look is dark, the terminals' included.
setting.appearance.connection_themes: Themes of connections and WSL distributions
setting.appearance.connection_themes.hel: A connection and a WSL distribution can each have a theme of their own for each mode (the connection in the connection manager, the distribution on the tab Themes): the panel - the list, the headers, the tabs - and its SSH or WSL terminal draw with it, so servers and distributions are told apart at a glance. Off: every panel draws with the window's theme; the connections and distributions keep theirs.
settings.colours.low_surface: The window's text is hard to read on its surface (contrast below 4.5:1).
settings.colours.low_terminal: The terminal's text is hard to read on its background (contrast below 4.5:1).
settings.themes.builtin_hint: A built-in theme does not change: Duplicate makes an own one of it.
settings.themes.in_use: A mode draws with this theme: choose another for it before deleting this one.
settings.themes.name: Name
settings.themes.created: Theme made; it opens in the editor.
settings.themes.file_help: Import reads a theme from this file; Export writes the marked theme into it, .rctheme added where the name has no such ending.
settings.themes.no_file: Name a file with its full path first.
settings.themes.imported_dropped: Theme "{name}" imported; colours this version does not know were left out: {tokens}.
settings.themes.conflict: An own theme is named "{name}" already.
settings.themes.editor_help: The window shows the theme while you edit it; Cancel brings back the colours of before, Save keeps the theme.
error.theme_wrong_mode: This theme is for the other mode.
error.theme_builtin: A built-in theme does not change; duplicate it to change the copy.
error.theme_in_use: A mode draws with this theme; choose another before deleting it.
error.theme_invalid: The theme does not fit: a name, known colours and #rrggbb each.
error.workspace_version: The workspace is of another version than this rCommander reads.
error.workspace_tabs: A panel of a workspace has 1 to 32 tabs and shows one of them.
error.workspace_terminal: The workspace's terminal does not fit: the terminal view needs one, with a known shell, distribution or connection.
error.workspace_location: A tab of a workspace shows a folder on this computer or on a server, never inside an archive.
error.workspace_connection: The connection is no longer in the connection manager.
error.workspace_theme: There is no such theme for this mode.
error.workspace_too_large: The workspace is too large (at most 64 KiB).
error.workspace_name: A workspace needs a name of at most 64 characters, without control characters.
error.theme_file_too_large: The file is too large for a theme (at most 64 KiB).
error.theme_file_invalid: The file is no rCommander theme.
error.theme_file_unknown_key: The file has an entry a theme does not have; it was not imported.
error.theme_file_version: The theme is of a newer version than this rCommander reads.
error.theme_file_colour: A colour of the theme is no #rrggbb; it was not imported.
setting.appearance.wsl_themes.help: Per WSL distribution a light and a dark theme: a panel on its share and its WSL terminal draw with it.
settings.themes.wsl_help: A panel on a distribution's share and its WSL terminal draw with the distribution's theme of the mode; Default draws with the window's. The switch Themes of connections and WSL distributions (tab Theme and window) turns them all off.
setting.panels.refresh_on_focus: Read the panels again on return to the window
setting.panels.refresh_on_focus.help: On: when you come back to rCommander from another program, every panel that shows a folder on a local drive or a WSL distribution is read again, so a file saved meanwhile appears. Cursor, selection and scroll position stay. Switching between rCommander's own windows reads nothing again. Servers and archives are never read again this way.
On: the return to the window also reads panels on mapped network drives and network shares (\\server\share) again. Off by default, since a slow server would be asked on every return. Works only while "Read the panels again on return to the window" is on.
settings.shortcuts.workspace.help: Choose the workspace, press Record key, then the key that applies it.
workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.empty: No workspace yet. New (Insert) makes one of the panels as they are now.
workspaces.keys: Enter applies and closes, Insert makes a new one of the panels, F2 renames, Delete or F8 deletes, Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down change the order.
workspaces.choose: Choose a workspace to edit it here, or make one of the panels as they are with New.
workspaces.field.name: Name
workspaces.captured: The workspace now holds the panels as they are.
inventory.title: Server inventories
inventory.help: An inventory plugin reads the hosts of NetBox, Proxmox or another system; rCommander keeps a folder of connections in step with them. Your own fields of a connection - credentials, login script, drive-bar mark - stay as they are, and a host that leaves the inventory is marked, never deleted.
inventory.no_plugin: No inventory plugin is installed or switched on (Settings, Plugins).
inventory.name: Name
inventory.token_hint: The token is stored in the vault and sent only to this address; the plugin never sees it. A new address or plugin forgets it.
inventory.never_synced: Not synced yet: Sync shows a preview first.
inventory.report: {created} new, {updated} changed, {unchanged} unchanged, {missing} no longer in the inventory, {skipped} left out
setting.inventory.refresh_minutes.help: How often each server inventory synced before is synced again; 0 syncs only when you ask (0-10080).
error.name_invalid: The name is empty, too long or holds a control character.
error.inventory_address_invalid: The address is empty, too long or holds a space.
error.inventory_slot_invalid: The plugin names a token slot rCommander cannot store.
error.inventory_plugin_missing: The inventory's plugin is not installed or is switched off.
error.plugin_secret_missing: The plugin asked for a token that is not stored; enter it in the inventory.
error.plugin_secret_target_not_allowed: The plugin tried to send its token where it may not go.
error.plugin_inventory_too_large: The inventory lists more than 10 000 hosts; nothing was changed.
error.duplicate: The inventory lists this host twice.
status.portable_ignored: The marker rcommander.portable beside the program was passed over: {reason} The data stays in your profile.
db.portable_question: Copy the database and the installed plugins into the folder data beside the program, and keep the data there from the next start on? On that drive, connection names, hosts, user names, host keys and the history are readable without a password; passwords and keys stay encrypted with the master password. To go back, delete rcommander.portable beside the program.
db.portable_running: Copying the database and the plugins...
db.portable_done: This copy is portable: its data is in {folder}. Restart rCommander to use it; until then changes still go to the old folder.
error.update.portable_macos: A macOS app cannot keep its data beside the program; its signed bundle would break.
error.update.portable_package_manager: A package manager installed this copy; its next upgrade would take the data folder with it. Unpack the zip or tar.gz package instead.
error.update.portable_not_writable: The program's folder cannot be written; a portable copy needs a folder of its own, not one like C:\Program Files.
error.update.portable_network_drive: The program's folder is on a network drive, where the database cannot be kept reliably.
error.update.portable_linked_data: The folder data beside the program is a link or junction; rCommander does not follow it.
error.update.portable_database_exists: A database exists in the folder data beside the program already; it is never overwritten.
error.update.portable_already: This copy keeps its data beside the program already.
search.archives_local_only: Archives are searched on the machine's own drives only; this panel shows a server or a device.
search.everything_missing: Everything is not running, or is older than 1.4: the search walks the folders.
setting.search.archives_default: Find files starts with Search archives ticked
setting.search.archives_default.help: On: Alt+F7 opens with Search archives ticked, so zip, 7z and tar files on local drives are searched like folders. Each search can still change it.
setting.search.everything.help: On: where Everything (voidtools, 1.4 or later) runs, Find files offers to take its candidates from Everything's index, also with ev: before the masks. Windows only.
error.archive_not_modifiable: This archive cannot be changed (a compressed tar, a single compressed file or a self-extracting archive); unpack it and pack it anew.
error.archive_encrypted: The archive holds encrypted entries; it is not changed.
error.archive_changed: The archive was changed by something else meanwhile; nothing was changed.
error.archive_in_use: The archive is open in another program and cannot be replaced; it stays as it was.
error.archive_not_local: Only an archive on a local drive can be changed, not one inside another archive or on a server.
error.not_enough_space: There is not enough space on the drive for the new archive beside the old one.

setting.ssh.forward_reconnect: Reconnect port forwards after a lost session

setting.ssh.forwards_in_status_bar.help: "Forwards: n" while some run; each one in its tooltip.

error.inventory_unlicensed: The inventory's plugin has no valid licence key; enter it on the plugin's page in Settings, Plugins. Nothing was asked of the inventory.

Importing a key also takes the certificate beside it. Off, keys log in alone and the agents' certificates are passed over.

error.ssh_certificate_not_yet_valid: The key's certificate is not valid yet and was not sent.
error.ssh_certificate_principal: The SSH server refused the key's certificate: it is not issued for this user.
setting.columns.auto_switch: Switch to a column set by folder
setting.columns.auto_switch.help: A panel entering a folder that a column set's folder mask matches shows that set; the first set in the list wins. A view chosen by hand stays until a folder of another set.
setting.columns.auto_default.help: What a panel shows in a folder no column set's mask matches, as Total Commander's default mode: the view stays unchanged, or the full or the brief view.

settings.columns.help: A column set shows the columns you choose; a right click on a panel's column header or the command palette shows one. The order decides whose folder mask wins.

setting.viewer.exif: Show a photo's EXIF beside the picture
setting.viewer.exif.help: Lister (F3) and Quick View (Ctrl+Q) offer the EXIF of a JPEG, PNG or WebP photo - camera, exposure, date, position - as a second view beside the picture; 7 switches between them. Only the EXIF block is read. Off: a photo shows the picture alone.

setting.rename.selection_dialog: Shift+F6 on several selected items opens a dialog
setting.rename.selection_dialog.help: When on, Shift+F6 with two or more selected files and folders opens the rename dialog with the mask *.*, as Total Commander does, so a mask such as *.old renames them all. When off, Shift+F6 always renames the item under the cursor in the list.
setting.panels.git_status: Git status in the file lists
setting.panels.git_status.help: Where rCommander runs git to mark changed, new and ignored files and to show the branch. Off (the default) runs git nowhere; Local drives on fixed and removable drives and in WSL distributions (only while the distribution runs); Also network drives adds network drives and shares. git runs only for a folder inside a repository, hardened against the repository's own configuration: no filter driver (Git LFS among them) and no fsmonitor runs, so an LFS file whose time changed may show as modified. Needs git 2.36 or newer. Only you can switch this on; an agent cannot.
setting.panels.git_ignored.help: On: entries a .gitignore excludes are drawn dimmed. Off: git is not asked for them, which is quicker in large repositories.
setting.panels.git_branch: Git branch in the status line
setting.panels.git_branch.help: On: a panel's status line shows the repository's branch with the commits ahead of and behind its upstream, or HEAD and the commit when it is detached.
setting.panels.git_program.help: The git that marks the file lists. Empty: the first git in the folders of PATH (absolute ones only), on Windows then Git for Windows in Program Files. In a WSL distribution its own /usr/bin/git runs. Only you can change this; an agent cannot.
keys.view_file_cursor_only: View only the file under the cursor
setting.files.associations.help: Commands by file type that Enter and the context menu run ahead of the system's association; F3 and F4 do not use them.
setting.files.associations_enabled.help: Off: Enter and the context menu use the system's association alone.
setting.files.associations_all_matches: Load extra commands from all matching types
setting.files.associations_all_matches.h: The context menu offers the named commands of every rule whose mask matches, not only the first's.
setting.viewer.step_through_selection: N and P step through the marked files
setting.viewer.step_through_selection.he: F3 with marked files: Lister steps only through those; Shift+F3 shows the file under the cursor alone.

keys.panel.toggle_watch: Switch the file watcher on or off
setting.panels.watch: Read the panels again when their folder changes
setting.panels.watch.help: On: a folder shown in a panel is watched, and a file created, deleted or renamed in it appears within about a second, as Total Commander's automatic refresh does. Cursor and selection stay. Only folders on this machine are watched; archives, servers and search results are not. Off by default.
setting.panels.watch_changes: Also when size, date or attributes change
setting.panels.watch_changes.help: On: a file that only grows or gets a new date also reads the panel again. Off by default, since a download in progress would read the panel over and over.
setting.panels.watch_network.help: On: folders on mapped network drives and network shares are watched too. Off by default, since some servers keep a connection open for each watched folder or stop reporting without notice.
setting.panels.watch_exclude.help: Drive letters such as DE, and a backslash (\) for every network path (\\server\share). Empty: every drive is watched.
setting.panels.watch_background: Read while another program is in front
setting.panels.watch_background.help: On: changes are shown while you work in another program. Off: a change is only noted, and the panel is read once when you come back.
setting.terminal.refresh_panels_on_promp: Read the panels again when a terminal command ends

On: when the shell of a local or WSL terminal is back at its prompt after a command, the panels showing local folders are read again, so a file the command made appears. Works without the file watcher; needs the shell integration. SSH terminals never read the panels.
error.remote_edit_too_many: 32 server files are open for editing already. Finish one (Done in the list of server files being edited) first.
error.remote_edit_unknown: This server file is no longer being edited.
error.remote_edit_program: This file would run as a program. Copy it to a local folder first (F5), or allow it in Settings > Programs.
error.remote_edit_not_a_file: This is no file that can be edited: a folder, or a link that leads nowhere or in a circle.
setting.remote_edit.upload: After a server file opened for editing is saved
setting.remote_edit.upload.help: F4, Enter and an external viewer on an SFTP, FTP or FTPS file open a local copy, watched for saves. Ask: each save asks whether to upload it (with a box to stop asking). Upload without asking: each save goes to the server at once, as Total Commander's "Automatically re-upload changed files".
setting.remote_edit.check_server_changes: Check the server's file before an upload
Before a copy goes up, the file on the server is looked at: if its size or time changed since it was opened, or it is gone, you are asked first - Overwrite, Upload as copy or Not now.
setting.remote_edit.open_programs: Enter opens programs on a server
setting.remote_edit.open_programs.help: Off, Enter refuses a server file that would run as a program (an extension of PATHEXT on Windows, an execute bit elsewhere): copy it first (F5). On Windows every fetched copy is marked as coming from the internet either way.

remote_edit.ask.server_gone: "{name}" is no longer on {server}. Upload your copy anyway?
remote_edit.ask.in_place: "{name}" on {server} has several links or another owner. The upload writes into the file itself, so links and owner stay - but a break may leave half a file.
remote_edit.ask.kept: A change to "{name}" from {server} was kept when rCommander last quit. Upload it, discard it, or decide later?
remote_edit.discard.title: Discard the change?
remote_edit.discard.text: "{name}" holds a change that is not on the server. Discard it with the copy?
remote_edit.list.title: Server files being edited
remote_edit.list.empty: No server file is open for editing.
quit.remote_edits: Changes not uploaded to their servers: {names}. The copies are kept and offered at the next start.

tabs.close_all_question: Close every other tab of this panel?
tabs.close_all_keep_locked: Close them, keep the locked tabs
setting.filters.programs.help: The extensions Ctrl+F11 shows as programs, separated by spaces. Outside Windows a file with an execute bit is a program too.
setting.tabs.filter_per_tab: Keep the file filter separately for each tab
setting.tabs.filter_per_tab.help: On, each tab keeps the file filter of Ctrl+F10, Ctrl+F11 and Ctrl+F12; off, the tabs of a panel share one, as in Total Commander before version 10.
setting.tabs.confirm_close_all.help: Close all tabs from a tab's menu or the menu Commands asks whether the locked tabs close too; off, it closes the unlocked ones at once.
setting.ignore_list.enabled.help: On, the names and paths of the ignore list never show in the file lists, the flat views, the search and the folder sizes, and copies and moves leave them where they are; deleting a folder names how many it holds.
setting.ignore_list.entries.help: One entry per line: a name or mask (*.bak) hides it in every folder; a path (%USERPROFILE%\AppData) hides that folder on this computer; \Path without a drive on every drive; a \ at the end only folders. At most 1000 lines.
setting.history.frequent_shown: Most visited folders in the history list
setting.history.frequent_shown.help: How many of the most visited folders Alt+Down lists below the folder history; the counts halve every 30 days. 0 shows none and counts nothing.

error.plugin_compare_too_large: The compare plugin listed more than 10 000 changes; nothing is shown.
setting.thumbnails.size.help: The side of a thumbnail in pixels, 32 to 512 (96 as in Total Commander). Ctrl and the mouse wheel over the thumbnails change it in steps.
setting.thumbnails.disk_cache.help: Thumbnails of local files are kept in your cache folder, so a folder shows them at once the next time. Files on servers, devices and in archives never go there.
setting.thumbnails.cache_mb.help: 16 to 4096. At the start the thumbnails used longest ago go once the cache is larger.
setting.thumbnails.remote: Thumbnails on servers, devices and in archives
setting.thumbnails.remote.help: Off: files over SFTP and FTP, on phones and inside archives show their icon, and nothing is read for a thumbnail. On: pictures up to 32 MiB are read whole; their thumbnails stay in memory only.
setting.thumbnails.explorer.help: PDFs, videos and documents get the thumbnail Explorer shows. This runs the thumbnail handlers other programs installed inside rCommander, on every file you look at. Off, those files show their icon.

setting.viewer.certificates: Show certificates and keys with their checks
setting.viewer.certificates.help: Lister (F3) and Quick View (Ctrl+Q) show a certificate, certificate request or key file (PEM, DER, OpenSSH, authorized_keys) as its checks and objects - validity, chain, whether a key belongs to its certificate, weak keys and signatures - as text and, on 7, as a tree. A private key is shown only by its type, size, encryption and fingerprint, never decrypted. Off: the file shows as it is.
setting.viewer.cert_expiry_warning_days: Warn this many days before a certificate expires
A certificate whose end is fewer days away is a warning in the certificate view's checks; 0 never warns.
